title: Knitted-on cast-on
subtitle: The simplest single-strand cast-on for complete beginners.
excerpt: The knitted-on cast-on works like a knit stitch: insert, wrap, draw through, and slip back. Slower than the long-tail method but straightforward for anyone who can work a knit stitch.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938). Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A single-strand cast-on that uses the knit stitch action to build each new loop and slips it back onto the left needle.

content.text: (abbreviated k-co) repeats the knit stitch action over and over to build the starting edge. Each new loop is slipped back onto the left needle rather than transferred to the right. The edge is softer and slightly loopier than the long-tail or cable cast-on, and the method is slow for large stitch counts, but it demands no tail calculation and no special hand position. Difficulty: beginner.
Make a slip knot on the left needle.
Insert the right needle into the slip knot as if to knit, wrap the yarn, and draw a loop through to the front. Do not drop the original stitch.
Slip the new loop from the right needle back onto the left needle. Two stitches are now on the left needle.
Repeat steps 2 and 3, each time inserting the right needle into the last stitch placed on the left needle, until you have the required count.

Many beginner knitting guides teach this method first because it requires only the knit stitch. It appears in older Weldon's patterns as the 'cast-on for plain knitters', where rows are kept short and the slow pace of building stitches is not a problem. The cable cast-on is strictly better for firm edges; use the knitted-on cast-on when you need stitches urgently mid-row and a cable needle is not at hand.

items.symptom: Each new stitch is looser than the last
items.cause: The working yarn is pulled less consistently with each pass
items.fix: Snug each new stitch to the same firmness before moving to the next. Counting aloud helps maintain a steady pace.
Cast on more snugly, or try the long-tail or cable cast-on for a firmer, more even edge.

items.symptom: Slipping the new loop twists it
items.cause: Turning the right needle at an angle when slipping back
items.fix: Keep the right needle parallel to the left when sliding the loop across. The leading leg should sit on the front of the needle.
